answer_translation_latex:
```latex
The algorithm:  
We will maintain an auxiliary heap. The auxiliary heap will hold some of the keys of the original heap, with pointers to the corresponding nodes in the original heap. Initially, we copy the root of the original heap to the auxiliary heap.  
At each step, we perform ExtractMax from the auxiliary heap. We print the element that was removed, \(x\). We insert its two children from the original heap into the auxiliary heap. We repeat this until \(k\) elements are printed.  

Correctness explanation:  
If the key of a node is not among the largest \(k\) keys, then it does not need to be printed, and necessarily its children do not need to be printed either. Note that at each step the auxiliary heap contains all the potential elements for printing, i.e., all the children (from the original heap) of the nodes that were printed. Every node whose parent will be printed will enter the heap itself, and every node whose parent will not be printed will not enter the heap. Therefore, the algorithm will print the \(k\) largest values, even in descending order.  

Runtime analysis:  
At each step, we remove one element from the auxiliary heap and insert two in its place. That means the size of the auxiliary heap is at most \(k+1\). Therefore, the time for a basic operation on the heap is \(O(\log k)\).  
Finding the two children is performed in \(O(1)\) time (because there is a pointer to the appropriate element in the original heap). Therefore, the total time is \(O(\log k)\).  
At each step of the run, three operations are performed on the auxiliary heap (one Extract and two Insert). There are \(k\) such steps. The total is \(O(k \log k)\).  
Therefore, the total runtime is \(O(k \log k)\).  
Note that in the last \(k/2\) steps, the heap is already of size at least \(k/2\), so the time for a basic operation on the heap is \(O(\log k)\), which means the total runtime is also \(O(k \log k)\), and hence \(O(k \log k)\).
```
